oracle: in an owned temporary root holding the seeded entries, run each step through the JSONL backend with compression none on the step's handle, a or b, each its own backend instance over the root: create, a write open, or the open handle's append, flush, or close; after each step list every file beneath the root with its text, an empty session.lock by its size
history: Version 1: 33 cases, written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran; both arms passed on their first run.

A Rust negative control that skipped the truncation still passed open-torn-tail-truncated-by-first-append, whose torn tail was a prefix of the row appended after it. Its tail became a longer torn ext/note row, and no outcome changed.

Version 2: 55 cases. Rust migrates an older generation at a write open, so the older-generation limit is removed and limit-older-generation became migrate-header-less, with TypeScript's exact message. An open step's message may hold a {src} placeholder for the source path its src field names, and an open step may be marked outside-domain. The 22 added cases and the changed one were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran; both arms passed on their first run.

Version 3: 61 cases. Rust takes the write lease as TypeScript does, so trees list session.lock, which both harnesses read only by its size, and a step may name a handle, a or b, each its own backend instance over the root. The 6 added cases and the session.lock entries of the existing trees were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran. Both arms passed on their first run.

Version 4: 63 cases. Rust runs the catalog's final check of a migrated log, so outside-domain-final-check became migrate-final-check-turn-order with TypeScript's exact message and no rust override, and 2 cases were added: a final-check refusal of a v0 source and a v2 TOOL_NOT_STARTED repair the final check admits. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran. Both arms passed without any expectation change.

Version 5: 64 cases. Rust writes numbers as JSON.stringify writes them, so encode-fraction-written, a fraction in free data, has no Rust limit, and limit-encode now witnesses the encode limit with a source member spelled 0.0; both were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 6: 69 cases. Rust ports TypeScript's encoding-mismatch refusal, so limit-opposite-encoding became encoding-mismatch-at-open with TypeScript's exact message, and a message may hold a {srcJson} placeholder, the step's src path as JSON.stringify spells it, which a create step may also name. Rust lays out Windows names as TypeScript does on POSIX, so limit-windows-name became three POSIX cases, con, nightly., and aux.txt, created and reopened in both arms, and a win32 case for nightly., the spelling a Windows writer can produce, where Rust keeps the windows-name limit. Two cases were added for the root check: the highest Zstd generation is named, and a flat file is refused first. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 7: 70 cases. Rust reads older-generation rows at any nesting depth, so migrate-v2-deep-tool-schema, a v2 request header whose row nests 207 levels through its MCP tool schema, migrates unchanged in both arms; it was written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 8: 73 cases. Rust ports TypeScript's flat-layout refusal, so the legacy-layout limit is removed: limit-legacy-layout became legacy-layout-flat-file-at-create with TypeScript's exact message, and legacy-layout-before-encoding-mismatch lost its rust override. The root check refuses only a regular file with the flat-layout suffix, as listSessionDirs does, and the id's flat names are probed by opening them, as rejectLegacyFlatArtifact does. session-directory-named-jsonl creates, reopens, and lists a Session directory nightly.jsonl; legacy-probe-finds-session-directory refuses the id nightly beside it at open and create; legacy-layout-file-refused-at-open keeps a flat file refused at open. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

cases.note: A Session without a cwd lives in _no-cwd; nothing exists until the flush.
The cwd / reads as one separator, which is stripped, leaving the slug root.
Each run of /, \, and : becomes one -, the leading one is stripped, and the trailing one stays before the closing --.
~ is escaped in the project key and the id, so an escape cannot be forged.
The whole segments . and .. are escaped, so neither names the project or root directory.
Escapes are per UTF-16 code unit, so the astral character becomes its two surrogates; the log text keeps the characters.

cases.platformReason: The 255-character project directory puts the log path past Windows' 260-character path limit.
cases.note: The slug is 249 letters and ~007E; its first 251 units end inside the escape.
